description: Accessibility ids this repo owns. Device flows and golden tests key off them, so they are a contract: stable forever, identical on all four platforms, and asserted by each app's spec-validation test. SDK ids (si_*) are NOT defined here — reference them from the SDK.

shell.description: Bottom nav token affordance, carries the countdown ring.
Starts a flow as a full-screen presentation.
Starts a flow nested inside the navigation shell.
The scenario drawer's own root, matching every other sheet.
shell.resolved: RESOLVED 2026-08-14. This id stays on the drawer root: screens.json already lists it among the drawer's own testIds, every other sheet names its root the same way (sample_country_sheet, sample_profile_switch_sheet), and Android already attaches it there — so nothing is renamed, which the stability rule forbids. The control that opens it takes sample_scenario_drawer_button, matching every other opener (sample_country_trigger opens sample_country_sheet). Only this description was wrong.

shell.description: Opens the scenario drawer. Automation-facing; the drawer is also reachable by deep link.
One drawer row; suffixed with the scenario id, e.g. sample_scenario_item_expiredToken.
One theme row; suffixed with the theme scenario id.

products.description: Profile + environment chip in the header.
Header avatar button; opens the profile-switch sheet (decision 2026-08-13).
One product card; suffixed with the product id, e.g. sample_product_card_smartSelfieEnrollment.
Remaining session time, as m:ss text.

verifications.description: One status filter chip; suffixed with the status, e.g. sample_filter_chip_attention.
The count inside a chip; suffixed with the status. Asserted after deletes.

Empty-list message on the verifications tab. Two texts behind one id: nothing submitted yet, versus nothing matching the active filter. Not in the design — added because the app seeds no rows, so a first launch would render a blank tab.
Country search matched nothing. No supporting line: the reader typed the query.
ID-type list is empty — either the country has no types, or the search matched none of them; the text says which.
One verification row; suffixed with index.
Select / Cancel action in the header.
Row checkbox in select mode; suffixed with index.
Selection bar shown instead of the nav bar.
Remove action in the selection bar.
Toast container. Used by verifications (removal + undo) and by profiles (the created confirmation).
The action inside a toast, whatever it is labelled: "Undo" on a removal, "Make active" on a created profile. The id is the contract, the label is not.

verificationDetails.description: One label/value row; suffixed with the field name, e.g. sample_detail_field_jobId.
Copy button on a field; suffixed with the field name.
Delete action in the app bar.
Shown when the route names a job this build has no row for, which a deep link can do. The jobId asked for is in the supporting line, because that is the whole diagnostic.

Pull-to-refresh container on the verification details screen, which is what the design draws in the processing state. Fetches GET /v3/status/{jobId} and rewrites the row. Always present, never conditionally hidden: a gesture that silently does nothing reads as a defect, so a refresh that cannot succeed reports why instead — no live scanned session, or a row never submitted under one (every fixture-token run). A row still processing is also refreshed automatically on entry, since that is the only status that can change.

userDetails.description: User details screen root — shown BEFORE the SDK flow starts.
One editable row; suffixed with the field, e.g. sample_user_details_field_firstName.
Primary action that launches the SDK flow.

kyc.description: One country row; suffixed with ISO code.
One ID type row; suffixed with the type id.

settings.description: Profile row at the top of settings; opens the profiles LIST, not the active profile's page.
Environment switch. ON is production; OFF is sandbox, which is the default. Read-only while the sandbox launch argument pins the run, so automation asserts the chip rather than driving this.
Smile to capture switch. ON means enhanced liveness OFF, so it and agent mode write different fields and cannot fight.
Consent screen switch → include/omit consent() in the flow.
One ABOUT/LEGAL navigation row; suffixed with the row id.

profiles.description: One profile row; suffixed with the profile id.
Create-profile row; opens the new-profile sheet, which returns to the list with the confirmation.
First name input; required before Create profile enables.
Last name input; required before Create profile enables.
One user-details default; suffixed with the field.
Saves the defaults AND makes the profile active — the design labels it "Make this profile active".

token.description: Simulate a successful scan — makes token flows testable with no QR source.

rules: One id per assertable element. If a flow needs to read it, it has an id.

Suffixed ids derive from other spec files — product ids from scenarios.json products, scenario rows from scenarios.json, field names from result-card.schema.json — so adding a product or field adds its ids automatically.
Never reuse an id for a different element, and never localise an id.
Counters and countdowns are exposed as their value in text form, so a flow can assert equality rather than parse prose.
Filter counts carry ids because 'the count dropped after a delete' is the assertion that proves the delete, not the toast.
